audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Gwen levels 3, 4-5 and first item and gave Aurora level 1, contradicting the page's own prose (early: "Level 1 is a wash"; mid: "Levels 4-6 are your peak") and the 55.56% win rate.
audit.why: Mirror reuse: audits/top/gwen__aurora.json already fixed this chart to Skill / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Gwen. Twofold Hex (900) and The Weirding (825) out-range Snip Snip!'s 450 cone; Gwen has no answer until Riftmaker plus a second item.
audit.corrected: Skill / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Gwen, with ratings re-set to match each side. diff FAV, diffRating 4/10 (inverse of the mirror's TRICKY 7.5/10).

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and the Level 6 entry names "Between the Worlds".
audit.why: Aurora's ultimate is Between Worlds (140/120/100s). Hallowed Mist is 22/21/20/19/18s — identical to Across the Veil's 22/21/20/19/18s, so her hiding tool and your escape come back together. Skip 'n Slash is 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s but is partially refunded whenever she hits something, so it is rarely truly down. Needlework is 120/100/80s at 1200 range.
audit.corrected: Real name and real numbers now carried in phases, breakdown.cooldowns and the report.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says Between Worlds makes Aurora untargetable, in four places. It does not.
audit.why: Riot's text for Between Worlds: she leaps, releases a damaging slowing shockwave, and creates a slow zone she can teleport across. The invisibility belongs to Across the Veil ("entering the spirit realm upon landing, becoming invisible"). Telling a player they are untargetable inside their own ult will get them killed standing in Needlework. Also missing: Hallowed Mist makes Gwen targetable only by enemies inside it, so a Twofold Hex fired from outside cannot pick her — you must be in the cloud or land it before she casts.
audit.corrected: Untargetability reassigned to Across the Veil's invisibility; Between Worlds described as a slow zone with a cross-zone teleport.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds, and nothing explains why MR beats armour here.
audit.why: A Thousand Cuts (P) heals Gwen off the bonus magic damage on every auto, so anti-heal matters from the first trade. Skip 'n Slash grants attack speed, range and magic damage on-hit — her damage is magic and attack-speed-scaled, which is why armour reads the trade wrong.
audit.corrected: whys[3] now names A Thousand Cuts and Oblivion Orb.

audit.whatIsWrong: Gwen is referred to as "him"/"his" in breakdown.mid, breakdown.wave, breakdown.trading, breakdown.feeding and breakdown.late, and "Snip Snip" is written without its exclamation mark in three places.
audit.why: Her Q is Snip Snip!. The pronoun errors come from a template.
audit.corrected: Pronouns and the ability name fixed.

You MUST close the game on your mid-game lead; do not try to scale a poke war against a true-damage hyperscaler who can just sit untargetable in Mist.

Riot's Data Dragon text for Across the Veil says nothing about a takedown reset, and I could not confirm it from the kit files — I removed the claim from whys[4] rather than restate it, but content.mid and full were left alone where it appears elsewhere. Please confirm whether the reset is real before it is re-added. Also: the full layer described Between Worlds as granting untargetability in four places; Riot's text gives it a slow zone and a cross-zone teleport, and the invisibility belongs to Across the Veil.
